stdout:
easy-call — HHH-20919 is a singleton bug in temporal collection key adjustment. No duplicates found.

The current Collection.adjustTemporalPrimaryKey() appends the period-start column to every unique key whenever the collection table has no primary key. Set.createPrimaryKey() creates a unique key for nullable set elements but deliberately skips generation when a user key already exists. Thus the subsequent general table-wide adjustment can modify keys that this collection did not create. Both main and 8.0 retain the TODO cited by the reporter.

Relevant code: hibernate-core/src/main/java/org/hibernate/mapping/Collection.java, Set.java, and boot/model/internal/TemporalHelper.java. SINGLE_TABLE marks the auxiliary ROW_START column for collection identity; other temporal strategies do not. UniqueKey.isExplicit distinguishes annotation constraints but is not sufficient proof that an arbitrary implicit key belongs to this collection, so prefer adjusting the exact inferred key at creation.

Blast radius is collection boot metadata and generated temporal DDL, not runtime mutation or public query API. Two-way implementation change, but existing schema is not automatically repaired; the test and migration note should make the corrected user-defined constraint columns explicit.

Implement a small domain-model regression on a temporal element collection with a user-defined unique constraint and no primary key. Prove named and unnamed explicit constraints retain only requested columns; prove nullable inferred set keys and nonnullable primary keys still contain period-start; use non-temporal controls. Prefer a package-private helper that adjusts a supplied identity Constraint, called for the actual inferred unique key and existing primary key, rather than scanning all table unique keys. Preserve naming and null/absent key behavior.

No fresh runtime reproduction has run yet; require failing-before/passing-after focused JDK25/H2 Actions, compilation/format checks and independent review. Test whether annotation second-pass timing exposes both named and unnamed constraints as expected, and whether HISTORY_TABLE/native strategies remain unchanged. Full database matrix remains deferred.
